newsitem.title: RUSSIA: PM tells troops to stay calm in Kremlin crisis.
newsitem.headline: PM tells troops to stay calm in Kremlin crisis.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Thursday ordered the defence and interior ministers to ensure their troops stay calm in the latest political crisis, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Tass said Chernomyrdin had asked the ministers and other security chiefs to summon their top officers and explain the "need to stay calm" during a war of words between Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov and security tsar Alexander Lebed.
Tass said Chernomyrdin made the remarks during a meeting of the government after which he intended to brief President Boris Yeltsin in detail over the row between Lebed and Kulikov.
He expressed the hope that the servicemen would "understand everything and sort things out in this situation".
Kulikov said on Wednesday that Lebed had been plotting a "creeping coup" while Yeltsin prepares for heart surgery. Lebed denied the accusations.

Chernomyrdin had earlier met top security and defence officials to look into the row. He told the cabinet that some of Kulikov's comments were justified, but dismissed his allegations that Lebed was plotting a mutiny or a coup d'etat.
The army has been dragged into Russia's political battles several time in 1990s.
In August 1991, Yeltsin led resistance to a failed hardline coup, among leaders of which were the then defence and interior ministers as well as the head of the KGB security police.
In October 1993, he sent army tanks to shell the White House parliament building following bloody riots in Moscow by supporters of the hardline parliament.

Army and interior ministry troops fought Chechen separatists on Yeltsin's orders for 21 months, suffering serious losses and many servicemen are deeply disenchanted over being dragged into an internal conflict.
